content.text:
`summarize()` now handles 200,000 orders in well under a second, and its output is unchanged. `npm test` passes, 4 of 4 tests. I did not time the new code separately. The 200,000-order test only asserts it finishes in under 1 second, and it did.

**Cause** (`src/report.js`): there were three quadratic costs. `seen.includes` scanned every earlier order id. `groups.find` scanned every customer. And `groups.sort(byRank)` re-sorted the whole leaderboard after every order.

**Fix:**
- Duplicate order ids are now tracked in a `Set`.
- Customer groups are looked up through a `Map`.
- Sorting happens once at the end, after dropping customers with no paid spend and before applying the limit.
- The ranking has no ties between different customers, because `customerId` is the last tie-break. So sorting once gives the same order as sorting after every order.
- A `NaN` customer id never matched an existing group under the old `===` lookup. I kept that behavior, so each such order still gets its own group.

**Tests added** (`test/report.test.js`):
- The original implementation is kept as a reference, and a test compares the new output against it with `deepStrictEqual` on 40 seeded random datasets at four limits. The data includes duplicate ids, refunds, pending orders, EUR and USD amounts, and tied spend and dates, so any change in output or ordering fails it.
- A performance test runs 200,000 orders and fails if it takes 1 second or more.
